$comment: Section catalog shared by every type. A type file lists which of these it uses (by id) and may add or override sections. checks: cards (>= 4 cards), mermaid (a diagram), table (a table), code (a shell command block), example (any non-diagram code block), table-complete (no empty cells in the section's tables).

about.must: How the parts are organised, the tag legend table when tags are used, conventions (date format, time zone, 'no secrets are reproduced; the document says where each value lives and who provides it').

summary.must: Card grid with 4-10 cards with the facts a newcomer needs first (goal, who uses it, scale, cadence, status, critical dependency...). When the sources name no owner or value for a card, write 'Em aberto' / 'Open' and add an open question. Close with an 'In one sentence:' line.

problem.must: Why it exists: the situation before, what goes wrong without it, what it delivers (numbered list of outcomes).

capabilities.must: Capabilities in business terms, each with who uses it and through what (API, screen, job, package). End with what it explicitly does not do.

context.must: Every neighbour: system, role, direction (calls us / we call / event), owner team. Users and external partners included.

flow.must: Mermaid flowchart of the main journey through all systems, then numbered prose walking through it.

journeys.must: One collapsible block per audience (end user, operator, support): what they see and do, step by step.

lifecycle.must: State diagram of the main entity (persisted status values with their numeric codes) and what moves it between states.

business-rules.must: Every rule enforced that a business person would care about (limits, validations, eligibility, time windows, time zones), each with the reason when known.

status.must: The first sentence carries the date ('Em 31/01/2026: ...'); never put the date in the heading. What is live and where, what is pending, the last relevant change.

faq-business.must: 3-12 questions a user, operator or approver would really ask, as collapsible blocks, answered from the sources (no invented questions about things the sources do not cover).

architecture.must: Mermaid diagram of runtime components (functions/containers/apps, queues, topics, databases, external systems) with the direction of every call/event; then a table of deployable units (name, type, trigger, runtime, timeout/memory when set). Name IaC resources by their logical id.

codebase.must: Solution/module layout, layering, the pattern every feature follows, key libraries and why.

data-model.must: Datastores, tables/collections with purpose and key columns, indexes and uniqueness, an ER diagram when there are >= 3 entities, migrations (tool, folder, how they run, list in order), shared/legacy databases read or written.

api.must: Every route with method and path on the same row: purpose, auth/permission, main responses. One collapsible block per route with sanitised request/response examples and error codes. Base URLs per environment.

messaging.must: Every queue/topic/stream: name per environment, producer, consumer, payload example, retry/DLQ policy, ordering and idempotency.

jobs.must: Every scheduled or background process. Translate triggers for humans: AWS cron() is UTC, so give the local time too; rate() has no wall-clock time ('every hour, counted from the deploy'); in-process schedulers (Hangfire, Quartz, Celery beat, cron libraries) use the server's time zone unless configured.

integrations.must: Every external dependency and what happens when it fails.

code-walkthrough.must: Flow by flow (one collapsible block each): entry point -> steps -> side effects, naming the files. Explain the non-obvious decisions in the code.

client-sdk.must: Published SDK/client: name, feed/registry, how it is generated and versioned, how consumers update.

configuration.must: (1) Overview table: kind of setting -> where it lives -> how it changes. (2) How configuration is loaded and its precedence. (3) Per environment, a collapsible block with every parameter/secret to create: environment, full name/path, value or source (never a secret value), type, who provides it, status. (4) Values fixed by IaC/build. (5) Feature flags. (6) Infrastructure changes still needed. (7) Deployment parameters and how each environment sets them. When a prefix exists but nothing loads it, list the keys and send the decision to open-questions.

security.must: Authentication and authorization (scheme, issuer, permissions per route/screen), runtime permissions (IAM), network placement, data protection (PII, encryption, retention), plaintext credentials found in the repo and the recommended action (never the values).

observability.must: Where logs go and a ready-to-use query, metrics, alarms, traces, dashboards, correlation ids, what a healthy run looks like.

run-local.must: Prerequisites with versions, local dependencies, local configuration, step-by-step shell commands (each block labelled as run, copied or derived), how to call/open it locally, seed data, common local problems.

tests.must: Strategy (unit/integration/e2e and what each covers), shell commands per suite (labelled as run, copied or derived), what each suite needs, manual test scripts for the main flows (Given/When/Then), last verified run (date + result).

deploy.must: Pipelines (file, trigger, stages, environments, approvals), versioning, how to deploy, how to roll back, post-deploy checks, data migrations and cut-over steps.

dev-decisions.must: ADR-style: decision, reason, alternatives rejected, consequence, source (commit/doc).

history.must: Timeline of significant changes built from git history, docs or the sources.

production-gaps.must: Checklist of what is still missing before (or after) going live, with owner.

risks.must: Risk, impact, severity, mitigation/status. Severity is the writer's judgment, stated as such: Alta/High (stops the work, financial, legal or security impact), Média/Medium (degrades or delays), Baixa/Low (inconvenience). Includes plaintext credential files, single points of failure, missing tests or controls, known bugs.

open-questions.must: Everything the sources could not answer, each with who can answer it. Never guess; put the gap here. Mark na only when there are none.

faq-technical.must: 3-12 questions a new engineer asks in week one, as collapsible blocks, answered with file refs.

troubleshooting.must: Symptom -> likely cause -> how to confirm (log query, metric, SQL) -> fix. Built from error handling, DLQs and known incidents.

glossary.must: Business terms, technical terms and acronyms used anywhere in the document.

references.must: Map of the documents, repos, dashboards, tickets and people this document was built from, plus a short note on how it is maintained (the .md is the source, the .html is generated by document-anything).
